_comment: Mutation testing for the score engine and the rest of packages/core. Coverage proves a line ran; this proves a WRONG line fails a test. packages/core is the right and only first target: it is pure TS with no I/O (core.md), so mutants are deterministic, and the Aura invariant is the highest-stakes logic in the repo. Run with `pnpm --filter @athanor/core mutation`.
_plugins_comment: Declared explicitly: Stryker's default plugin discovery globs node_modules and does not follow pnpm's symlinked layout, so the runner is installed and resolvable but not auto-loaded.
_thresholds_comment: `break` is the CI gate (.github/workflows/mutation.yml) and is set just under the measured score — 90.59% on the first run, 91.41% after killing the four Aura-path survivors it found, 96.73% after the survivor sweep — never aspirationally, because a threshold nobody can meet becomes a red job people learn to ignore. Ratchet UP as tests improve, never down (core.md precedent, same rule as the coverage floors).
_survivors_comment: The survivors still reported are NOT a backlog: each was read against its source and is either an equivalent mutant (no input distinguishes it), unreachable code the type system requires, or reachable only from data a DB constraint forbids. Every one is documented at its site — grep -i 'equivalent mutant' in src/ finds them. The clusters: six are the mutually-masking layers of highlight.ts's tokenizer, two its loop bounds, three the epsilon/tie-break comparisons in display.ts's reduce. Do NOT write a test to chase these — a test that cannot fail against the original asserts nothing, and the #4 review already caught seven of those. But do NOT assume the list is closed either: the first review of this file wrongly called highlight.ts's empty-normalized-token guard equivalent, and it was in fact a killable guard over an infinite loop, flagged independently by v8 branch coverage. Cross-check a claimed equivalence against the coverage report before trusting it. If the score drops below break, suspect a NEW survivor.
